sketches.title: Chat Court
sketches.premise: The group chat is now a courtroom, and every turn posts one piece of evidence that defeats the claim currently on trial. The first player states a claim; the next player must answer it with a standing fact, object, or witness.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new exhibit directly disproves, exposes, or makes the standing claim impossible; dodging it, merely surviving it, repeating it louder, or offering a bigger version of the same claim loses.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "Exhibit: what it is, and how it wrecks the claim." Example: against "I never ate the cake," post "Exhibit: the frosting on your nose; it catches you red-handed."
sketches.first_card: Claim: "Nobody saw me take the last slice."

sketches.title: Reply Guy Chain
sketches.premise: A message lands in the group chat, and each player replies with a single everyday thing that changes what the message can do. Your reply must act on the previous reply, not merely comment from the sidelines.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the reply blocks, fixes, exposes, reverses, or redirects the standing message; silence, escape, endurance, and a louder or larger copy of it do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "I reply with [thing], which [specific action on the last message]." Example: against "A rumor spreads," post "I reply with a screenshot of the source, pinning the lie to its author."
sketches.first_card: Message: "The secret is spreading through the chat."

sketches.title: Admin Powers
sketches.premise: One player posts a chat problem, and the other answers with a single moderation power or chat feature that handles it. The winning reply must visibly change the standing problem, as if the group had handed you the controls.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the feature directly removes, limits, reveals, or corrects the problem; merely leaving, waiting it out, making it bigger, or using a related feature without an effect loses.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "I use [feature] to [directly affect the problem]." Example: against "A flood of insults fills the chat," post "I use mute, silencing the flood without deleting the whole room."
sketches.first_card: Problem: "A spammer keeps posting the same message every second."

sketches.title: Caption Combat
sketches.premise: A strange image is dropped into the group chat, and each turn adds one caption that defeats the meaning of the caption before it. Your caption must be a thing or scene that makes the previous caption look false, harmless, or impossible.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new caption directly undercuts the standing caption through a clear real-world contradiction or consequence; a mere joke, escape, tougher copy, or vague change of subject loses.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "Caption: [scene], making the last caption [false or powerless]." Example: against "The dog guards the treasure," post "Caption: the dog asleep while the cat walks off with it, making the guard useless."
sketches.first_card: Image: a tiny umbrella floating in a swimming pool.

sketches.title: Voice-Note Brawl
sketches.premise: The chat is trading voice notes, but every note must be answered by a sound-making thing that defeats the sound just posted. You are not acting out a whole story: you name one standing source of sound and what it does to the previous noise.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new sound directly drowns, stops, exposes, or transforms the standing sound; hiding from it, being quieter somewhere else, or becoming a bigger version of it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "I am [sound source], [action], so the last sound [specific result]." Example: against "A baby screams," post "I am a fire alarm, piercing the scream and forcing everyone to notice the room's danger instead."
sketches.first_card: Voice note: "A mosquito whines beside your ear."

sketches.title: Poll Position
sketches.premise: The group chat runs a poll, and each turn posts one everyday choice that defeats the current winning option by making its victory impossible or pointless. A choice must act on the option in front of it, not merely be another preference.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks whether the new choice directly cancels, replaces, reveals the flaw in, or makes the standing choice lose; refusing to choose, waiting it out, choosing a larger copy, or changing topics loses.
sketches.move_shape: Post: "I choose [option], which beats [last option] by [clear consequence]." Example: against "Everyone votes for a secret plan," post "I choose public rules, which beat the secret plan by making its hidden terms unacceptable."
sketches.first_card: Winning choice: "Meet at midnight in the abandoned house."
